title: New York, New York
analysis_notes: Tseng stands rigidly at the center of a confetti-strewn avenue while parade crowds form receding walls and New York towers rise symmetrically behind him.

His gray suit, glasses, and controlled frontal stance separate from the dispersed spectators; the tiny centered body appears both official and conspicuously out of place within monumental civic space.
teaching_use: Study how a repeated persona, central axis, public event, and architectural perspective can turn self-portraiture into social performance.
anti_imitation: Costume and deadpan pose are not free-floating visual jokes; identify the work's critique of cultural authority, stereotype, and belonging, and disclose performance rather than implying candid reportage.

title: Pantheon, Rome
analysis_notes: The Pantheon's curved wall and coffers fill the frame with near-frontal symmetry, while small tourist groups spread unevenly across the lower band and a red-clad figure holds the right side.
Architecture supplies the dominant repeating grid and scale, but human spacing, pauses, and gaze directions prevent the interior from becoming an empty elevation study.
teaching_use: Study how a fixed architectural structure can contain distributed human activity and how small figures reveal both scale and patterns of looking.
anti_imitation: Symmetry alone can flatten a place into design; wait for meaningful human intervals and do not treat visitors merely as scale markers when their behavior is part of the subject.

title: Covered Car—Long Beach, California
analysis_notes: A sheet-wrapped car forms a pale horizontal body between two dark palm trunks, with its wheels and identity concealed while hard sunlight casts a long black ground shadow.
The repeated palms, low building bands, and compressed tonal blocks turn an ordinary parked vehicle into an ambiguous object without removing its suburban setting.
teaching_use: Use it to study how concealment, silhouette, and environmental repetition can make a familiar object newly readable while context prevents pure abstraction.
anti_imitation: An obscured object is not automatically mysterious or socially meaningful; ensure that form, place, and sequence support the interpretation rather than relying on vagueness.

title: Girl in Her Circus Costume, Maryland, 1970
analysis_notes: A girl stands frontally in a decorated costume, centered against a dark tent wall while a pale cape pulls strongly to the right in the wind.
The square print includes grass, tent ropes, and an uneven fabric edge, so formal pose and moving garment remain visibly attached to the provisional circus environment.
teaching_use: Study how a simple frontal portrait can gain motion and setting from fabric, weather, and imperfect background edges without adding props.
anti_imitation: Do not treat costume or difference as an invitation to exoticize a child; consent, guardian involvement, caption precision, and the subject's dignity take priority over visual strangeness.

title: Barber Shop, Southern Town
analysis_notes: Four men are spaced across the wooden storefront—two at the dark doorway, one standing between openings, and one seated near the barber-shop door—each holding a distinct relation to the threshold.
Weatherboards, curb, wires, windows, and multiple hand-painted signs create horizontal and vertical order, while the figures interrupt rather than decorate the facade.
teaching_use: Study how architecture, intervals between people, doorway depth, and signage can make a group portrait without arranging everyone into a conventional cluster.
anti_imitation: A formal facade view can hide unequal social conditions behind apparent neutrality; preserve location, names where known, and the photographer-subject power context.

title: County of Sutherland, Scotland, 1988
analysis_notes: A green hillside scattered with gray rocks rises gently beneath a large clouded sky, with no singular peak, building, person, or dramatic light selected as the subject.
The image's attention is distributed through small color and texture changes across the slope; the low horizon leaves weather and terrain in quiet balance rather than climax.
teaching_use: Study how a landscape can sustain attention through distributed detail, modest color differences, and patient framing without a dominant landmark.
anti_imitation: Ordinariness is not achieved by photographing carelessly; edge relationships, horizon height, depth, weather, and descriptive precision must still create a deliberate visual field.

title: Lightning Fields 138
analysis_notes: Bright electrical nodes and branching traces float in a deep black field, with one large orb above and a denser cluster below linked by faint dotted and filament-like paths.
Without ordinary scale or horizon, the image shifts among lightning, cells, stars, and diagrams; its visual force comes from recorded physical process rather than photographed scene.
teaching_use: Use it to study how process, contrast, repetition, and scale ambiguity can become subject, and why technique should be understood as meaning rather than an effect preset.
anti_imitation: High-voltage experimentation is hazardous and requires expert equipment and protocols; do not attempt the process casually or claim a camera-less trace is documentary depiction of a natural scene.

title: Vile, Gothenburg, Sweden
analysis_notes: Muholi's face and upper body emerge centrally from black, with luminous painted bands wrapping head, shoulders, and torso into a graphic structure while the eyes meet the lens.
Extreme tonal separation suppresses ordinary setting and turns repeated stripes into both costume and frame; the mouth, nose, and gaze remain distinct rather than dissolving into pattern.
teaching_use: Study how controlled tonal range, surface pattern, and direct gaze can make self-representation formally forceful without relying on environmental description.
anti_imitation: Darkening skin, body paint, and culturally charged materials are not transferable style recipes; interpret them through Muholi's self-authored visual activism and never reproduce identity markers without ownership and context.
